raw_response:
I will do it the simple way, close to what people around me do, because I am old and I only farmed one year. I will not play clever with it. On my 5.5 mu, I will keep most land in wheat-maize because that is the steady road here, and I will leave a smaller piece for cotton. Wheat and maize feed the year better, and cotton can make some cash if the price is not bad. I have well water, so I will not let the field stay dry at the key time. I would rather spend a little more on fertilizer than watch the crop turn thin and yellow. What I saw in nearby fields is this: wheat needs the strongest base, maize must not be starved after wheat harvest, and cotton needs more watching for insects. I will use improved seed for wheat, hybrid seed for maize, and improved cotton seed, because if the neighbors get a fuller stand from that, I will follow them. For the 4 mu that goes wheat then maize, I will fertilize wheat a bit heavier, water it about 3 times, and spray about 2 times. After wheat comes off, I will seed maize quickly on the same 4 mu, keep fertilizer ready, water 2 times if rain is not enough, and spray about 2 times. On the 1.5 mu cotton piece, I will plough it, use enough fertilizer so it does not run out later, water about 3 times, and spray more often because cotton insects can eat money fast.
